title: Palantir Looks Like a Consulting Company. Its Numbers Tell a Different Story.
detail:
Palantir Looks Like a Consulting Company. Its Numbers Tell a Different Story.
Adam Spatacco, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:35 AM MDT 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

There is a criticism of Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) that refuses to go away. For all the praise surrounding its artificial intelligence (AI) software, Palantir sends engineers directly into customer organizations to solve problems. On the surface, this sounds like consulting.

While there is some truth to that comparison, Palantir's forward deployed engineers work alongside customers rather than simply handing them a software toolkit and walking away. Focusing on this process misses what Palantir is actually selling -- and, more importantly for investors, the economics of the business.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

If Palantir were really a consulting firm disguised as an AI company, its financial statements would eventually expose that. Instead, they're telling almost the exact opposite story.

Image source: Getty Images.
Palantir's engineers are not traditional consultants

Palantir calls its sales approach forward deployed engineering. The idea is straightforward: engineers go directly into organizations, learn how those businesses operate, integrate Palantir's technology with their systems, and build data workflows around real-world problems.

Although this has consulting characteristics, there's an important difference. A traditional consulting firm like Accenture, Booz Allen Hamilton, or McKinsey, primarily monetize the time and expertise of its employees. Palantir's engineers are deploying the company's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), a suite of software programs that can be used across an entire organization in different departments.

Palantir's AIP Bootcamps reinforce the business model. Prospective customers can demo AIP and work directly with Palantir to build use cases in a matter of hours or days. Once customers see how the software works against their own pain points, Palantir can expand the relationship quickly -- keeping customers sticky in the process.

Palantir's financials look nothing like a consulting firm

Palantir's second-quarter results were remarkable. Total revenue surged 93% year over year to $1.94 billion. U.S. commercial revenue accelerated 149% to $764 million, while U.S. government revenue climbed 90% to $809 million.

During the quarter, Palantir closed 220 deals worth at least $1 million, including 73 worth at least $10 million. Meanwhile, U.S. commercial remaining deal value (RDV) increased 124% to $6.24 billion.

Key Takeaways

Palantir stock has gained 45% over the past three months to close at $194 on October 7, 2026, after Q2 revenue rose 93% YoY to $1.935B.

Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy on October 8.

The Street counts 19 buys, 1 outperform, 9 holds, 1 no opinion, 1 underperform, and 1 sell, with a $200 mean target sitting 3% above the October 7 close.

TIKR's mid-case model values Palantir stock at $1,389 by December 2030, implying a 615.8% total return, or 59.2% a year.

Palantir Stock Is Up 45% in Three Months After a 93% Revenue Quarter
PLTR Stock Price: 3-Months (TIKR)

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) stock has gained 45% over the past three months, closing at $194 on October 7, 2026. The sharpest move came after the company reported second-quarter revenue of $1.935 billion on August 3, up 93% year-over-year.

The stock opened the period at roughly $134 and slipped into the low $120s through July. Then the report landed, and shares gapped to the low $160s the next session.

CEO Alex Karp set a growth goal in his prepared remarks on the Q2 earnings call: "I am driving the business to grow at a rate equal or above to what we have in U.S. commercial for the next 18 months." U.S. commercial revenue had grown 149% in the quarter, and the same call raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.15 billion to $8.158 billion.

Palantir stock reached the mid-$180s in late August, slid to the mid-$160s by mid-September, and then climbed to $187 by September 30. Two infrastructure deals came during that stretch:

On September 8, Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner.

Armada became Palantir's inaugural Certified Modular Data Center Partner on October 1, pairing its Galleon modular data centers with Palantir's Sovereign AI Operating System.

On October 8, Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir stock to buy from neutral with a $230 target, and shares traded up 3.7% at $201 early in the session.

Across the chart, the stock went from roughly $134 in early July to $194 on October 7, with the July dip and the August 3 gap in between.

Palantir Stock's Mean Target Rose 9% While Shares Gained 66%
PLTR Stock Street Analysts Target (TIKR)

Nineteen analysts rate Palantir stock a buy, alongside one outperform, nine holds, one no opinion, one underperform, and one sell. The mean price target rose 9% to $200 from $183 on June 30, while the stock gained 66% from its $117 close that day. The mean now sits 3% above the October 7 close.

TIKR's Model Values Palantir Stock at $1,389 by the End of 2030
PLTR Stock Valuation Model Results (TIKR)

Using TIKR's advanced valuation model, I ran a mid case with revenue growing 57% a year, a net income margin of 48.4%, EPS growth of 59.5% a year, and the P/E shrinking 6.7% a year. Growth sits close to the last year's 56.2%, but the margin is a big step up from 35.0%, and the multiple shrinks after expanding 15.5% over the past year. I kept growth well under the 82% the company guided for 2026 because Karp's target covers 18 months, not five years.

Defense stock and artificial intelligence company Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) defied today's market downturn to rise 3% through 9:50 a.m. ET Thursday morning.

You can thank Goldman Sachs for that.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Goldman Sachs loves Palantir stock

Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded Palantir stock to "buy" with a $230 price target, as StreetInsider.com reports today. The rapidly rising growth stock, says Borges, did $6.2 billion in revenue over the last 12 months, has already reached an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of $8 billion, and is growing revenue at 100% per year.

Investors are valuing Palantir stock at 80 times trailing sales -- and twice that for price-to-earnings. This gives the stock a PEG ratio of about 1.6x, which is challenging, but not entirely indefensible, assuming Palantir can maintain its growth rate.

What's next for Palantir stock

But can Palantir keep growing sales at 100% per year? Borges argues it can, because the artificial intelligence market is approaching a new "step function" in which sovereign AI systems and "bespoke applications" (both built and owned entirely by their builders, rather than rented from other companies) provide a new market to grow in. Borges sees Palantir as a leading force in this market as it deploys "artificial intelligence forward-deployed engineers," or AI FDEs -- software agents built by Palantir -- to help build these systems.

The analyst further points out that Palantir stock is cheaper on a price-to-free cash flow basis than on P/E alone -- which is true. Free cash flow at the company runs about 10% ahead of reported net income. On an enterprise value-to-free cash flow-to-growth basis, Palantir scores closer to a 1.4x ratio.

Palantir still isn't a cheap stock, but Goldman's right: It's at least a little cheaper than it looks.

Palantir shares rise over 3% after Goldman Sachs upgrade
Proactive
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 8:30 AM MDT 1 min read
PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies Inc (NYSE:PLTR) shares were trading over 3% higher on Thursday morning as investors responded to Goldman Sachs upgrading the stock to 'buy' from 'neutral'.

The analyst said Palantir is seeing a step change in the depth of its addressable market, driven by demand for sovereign artificial intelligence(AI), bespoke software development and specialized industry sales.

The upgrade suggests Goldman expects Palantir to secure deeper and more customized customer engagements as organizations seek AI systems tailored to their data, operations and national requirements.

The investment bank said recent industry discussions indicated the stock was positioned for another phase of outperformance into 2027, supporting the more bullish view on Palantir's growth prospects.

Goldman's assessment also addresses concerns about whether Palantir's Forward Deployed Engineer model, which uses engineers to work closely with customers on customized deployments, can scale as the business expands.

The firm's report comes as Palantir operates at an annualized revenue run rate of about $8 billion and has been growing at roughly 100%, according to the research cited in the source material.

The upgrade also highlights Palantir's Ontology technology, which organizes enterprise data and processes, potentially allowing the company to become more deeply embedded in customer operations than seat-based software platforms.

Shares of Salesforce and ServiceNow were little changed, suggesting the Goldman view differentiates Palantir's customized AI deployments from packaged workflow software sold primarily through user subscriptions.

However, the upgrade does not resolve the long-running debate over Palantir's valuation, leaving future earnings and revenue growth to justify the premium investors have placed on the stock.

Tokenization platform Securitize is bringing a dozen of the biggest U.S. stocks to crypto traders, launching tokenized equities backed one-to-one by real shares, with Solana as the first network.

Announced Wednesday, the new Securitize Stocks product opens with security entitlements to 12 widely held names, including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Google, Tesla, Meta, Amazon, Netflix, Circle, Strategy and Palantir.

Myriad: How high will Nvidia go? Click to make your prediction.

The tokens will initially trade on Securitize's registered broker-dealer platform on Solana, settling in the USDC stablecoin, and will be available to eligible investors in the U.S., the European Union, and other permitted jurisdictions.

What sets the offering apart, the company said, is what sits behind each token. Rather than simply tracking a stock's price, as many offshore tokenized-equity products do, each Securitize Stock is backed one-to-one by an underlying share and represents a security entitlement under the Uniform Commercial Code, preserving investor rights and economic benefits like dividends and, where applicable, voting. The shares backing the tokens won't be lent out, and holders can convert their entitlements into actual registered shares where an issuer supports it.

"Tokenized stocks should give investors more than a price on a wrapper that tracks a stock and is only offered offshore," said Carlos Domingo, Securitize's chairman and CEO, framing the aim as bringing equities onchain "without leaving behind the ownership, investor protections and market infrastructure that make U.S. capital markets work."

Trading infrastructure is still expanding. At launch, liquidity will run through Securitize's Solana-based automated market maker, with Jump Trading serving as market maker and trading available during extended hours before a planned move to 24/7.

The release names a roster of partners, including Ripple Prime and Aave, as the asset becomes usable across onchain lending and collateral markets.

Securitize Begins Trading on NYSE as Tokenized Shares Land on Solana, Avalanche

The launch lands in a fast-accelerating race to put stocks on blockchain networks. Securitize's own shares have traded on Solana since its NYSE listing in July, while the SEC's "innovation exemption" opened a compliant path for tokenized stocks, and rivals from Coinbase to the NYSE and an OKX-ICE venture have moved into the space.

Securitize said its tokens are expected to trade on the NYSE's planned 24/7 venue and the OKX-ICE tokenized-securities venue, though neither has launched.
